evidence:
Reviewed every criterion description (2 gate, 41 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual) for a description that states several legs then waives some by judge choice. Per the skill's known false positive and the internal annotation, conjunctive whole-flow bundles are not defects here; every functional/polish binary ends 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.', which makes the listed legs conjunctive, and cross-ownership sentences (e.g. hro_arrive_bottom 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move', hro_undo_restores 'The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict', hro_drafts, hro_candidate_view, hro_candidate_linked, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_failed_send) move a leg to a named sibling rather than waiving it. Alternative-compliance clauses that remain one bar: hro_gate_render 'a refusal message is welcome but not required'; hro_move_one_stage/hro_reject_hired/hro_mgr_other_job 'hiding it is optional' with server refusal still required; hro_reject_reason location list; hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes' (same three observables); hro_stale_refused name-or-identifier; hro_notes 'not offered ... or is refused'; hro_pol_failed_send abort-or-offline; hro_pol_session_resume prompt-on-its-own; visual likert rows each have one 5-anchor scale. hro_add_candidate/hro_job_open 'wherever the app shows card/job details' are not vacuous because rules section 3 requires openable card details and hro_candidate_view grades team.

INSTANCE 1 (defect): tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23 hro_pol_live_board (weight 3 of 12 polish weight): 'scroll the page, or the board's scroll container if the page itself does not scroll, so it is not at the top; if neither scrolls at this viewport, add cards until one does, or record that no scroll exists and judge the other legs.' ... 'Fails if the update closes the details, clears or changes the note, moves focus or resets scroll.' When neither scrolls at the viewport (likely: polish/prompt.md:16 recommends a job with three cards), the description offers two alternatives, so the full-credit bar is either five legs including scroll preservation or four legs with scroll waived, at the judge's discretion. Scroll preservation is a public rule (hireops_rules.md section 5: an update must leave 'how far they have scrolled'), so the waiver drops a graded public behaviour by judge choice, not by an observed fact about the app.

INSTANCE 2 (Note, not counted as defect): tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:389 hro_candidate_private first forbids any candidate-received response containing 'board positions ... a rejection reason ... activity, including while Tomas's card is rejected', then accepts 'the replayed board and Activity reads are refused or answered with only that candidate's own data'. Read in isolation the second clause could admit an Activity reply holding Tomas's own rejection line (own data, but forbidden by the first clause); the closing conjunctive catch-all and protocol K ('answered with only Tomas's own data and none of the staff data', functional/prompt.md:43) resolve this to one bar, and the golden (index.js:171-176) returns only id/job_title/team/status/thread summary. Wording could still be tightened; rules section 7 says board/Activity 'are refused to candidates', which is a coverage/leniency matter for other rows.

No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'), so how the judge actually resolves Instance 1 is unmeasured.
counterexample: Broken app that passes under one reading: the board fits the 1280-wide desktop viewport vertically with the three recommended cards, and every live update re-renders the root so window/container scroll snaps back to 0. Judge path A adds cards until the page scrolls, observes scroll reset after Mei Lin's move, and scores hro_pol_live_board 0; judge path B, equally permitted by the text, 'record[s] that no scroll exists and judge[s] the other legs' and awards full weight 3. Conversely a conforming app gets the same score either way, so the variance falls only on the defective app and depends on judge choice.
suggested_fix: In hro_pol_live_board make the fallback sequential and fact-based: 'if neither scrolls, add cards (through ordinary UI) until the page or board scrolls; only if adding cards cannot make either scroll, record that and judge the other legs' (optionally also add 'answered with only that candidate's own data and none of the data listed above' to hro_candidate_private).
